maria-infra: :rotating_light: Rack aps4b-rack7 reporting repeated NVMe controller timeouts and post-boot hang on 6 nodes. Kernel oops + correctable ECC counts climbing. Starting triage.
aks-ops-bot: Alert: probe failure threshold crossed for aps4b-rack7 NVMe controller errors (6 nodes). https://ops.internal/alerts/1977771234 :rotating_light:
tony-oncall: Oncall here — which services are being impacted and do we need to engage support rotations?
maria-infra: Mostly batch jobs and low-priority Dedicated queues. Hosted API p95 in eu-west-1 up ~120ms since 02:10 UTC but still within SLO for now. 2 nodes are in a boot loop, 4 more showing degraded IO.
lina-sre: Can we cordon + drain the two looping nodes first to stop churn? Use `kubectl drain` with ignore-daemonsets for GPU pods.
maria-infra: Doing that now.
```bash
# cordon + drain example
kubectl cordon node-aps4b-07-45
kubectl drain node-aps4b-07-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60
```
maria-infra: Started drains on node-45 and node-46. Rebalancer will move allocations; I'll follow up with capacity impact.
deepak-hw: NVMe controller logs look like a firmware crash loop similar to the batch we saw last year. Suggest a quick `nvme fw-log` and attempt a reflash before RMA. RMA lead time is ~3 business days; spares in region are limited.
maria-infra: Pushing the nvme logs below (stripped):
```
[ 12.345678] nvme nvme0: I/O 1234 QID 0 timeout: completion entry lost
[ 12.345689] nvme nvme0: controller reset failed: -110
[ 12.346000] Correctable ECC errors increasing: device nvme0, sector 0x1f4a3
```
aks-ops-bot: Notice: eviction scheduler engaged for aps4b-rack7. Estimated transient GPU capacity reduction 18% while rebalancing.
jess-product: FYI — product side: if we expect sustained tail impact we should enable fallback routing to eu-central and switch critical routes to the smaller quantized model variant to limit customer-facing latency. Can flip a flag if ops approves.
lina-sre: Proposed remediation plan (short):
1) Cordon + drain the two boot-loop nodes (in progress).
2) Attempt firmware reflash on the 4 degraded nodes during off-peak window (22:00-02:00 UTC).
3) If reflash fails, schedule onsite controller swap for the two boot-loop nodes tomorrow 09:00 UTC.
4) Update routing to avoid aps4b-rack7 for non-critical allocations for 24h.
Expected capacity impact: ~15-20% for ~6 hours during reflash/drain operations.
ton y-oncall: Schedule works for me. Who's the owner for the onsite swap and field ops coordination?
deepak-hw: I'll own the RMA and field ops coordination. Onsite tech ETA 09:00 UTC tomorrow. Inventory check: 2 replacement controller assemblies available in our europe pool; if more needed we'll air-freight from us-west (cost will spike).
maria-infra: Drains completed for node-45 and node-46 :white_check_mark:. Logs uploaded to s3://redwood-logs/aps4b/rack7/1977771234/ . Kicking off firmware reflash on node-47 now.
```bash
# nvme firmware reflash (example)
nvme fw-download /dev/nvme0 --fw=/tmp/nvme_fw.bin && nvme fw-commit /dev/nvme0 -l 0
```
lina-sre: If flash fails, I'll patch the allocation policy to add `avoid_racks: ["aps4b-rack7"]` for 24h and open a routing rollout.
jess-product: I'll prepare the fallback model routing flag and draft a status update for customers if we see >10% error/latency regressions.
maria-infra: Current status: 2 nodes replaced in-schedule, 3 nodes still undergoing reflash, 1 node queued for RMA. Will update when flash completes or if reflash fails. :wrench: :package:
